rawItems.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan 2026-2046 Examination Report Published
rawItems.meetingTitle: Independent Examiner's Report for Huntingdonshire District Council and Ramsey Town Council
rawItems.summary: An independent examination of the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan 2026-2046 has concluded that the Plan meets the Basic Conditions, subject to recommended policy modifications. The report, dated 25 August 2026, recommends that the modified Plan proceeds to a referendum. It confirms the Plan was prepared by Ramsey Town Council for the designated Ramsey Neighbourhood Plan Area, covers the period 2026-2046, and addresses the development and use of land.

items.title: Reform councillor complains to Parliament over MP’s response to 199-home plan
items.content: A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. items.title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
items.content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. items.title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
items.content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.

items.title: Plans submitted for four-caravan traveller site on land near Ramsey
items.content: Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home."
